description: The WHEN OTHER arm of PROCESS-ENTER-KEY's ordered EVALUATE TRUE at :437-442, reached only when all three of MONTHLYI, YEARLYI and CUSTOMI satisfy '= SPACES OR LOW-VALUES'. Because EVALUATE is ordered and the first match wins, this case also pins the ORDER of the three arms above it - :213 MONTHLYI, :239 YEARLYI, :256 CUSTOMI - since a mis-ordered or fall-through EVALUATE would have matched one of them instead of dropping to the last arm. That is gate G30, and it is why all ten received items are declared explicitly blank in mapFields at their copybook widths rather than left to the request's initialisation: the premise of the case is stated, not assumed (practice B8). None of the six date parts nor CONFIRMI is examined on this path - the outer EVALUATE falls straight through to :437 before any date edit is reached. The arm then moves the :438 literal to WS-MESSAGE, raises WS-ERR-FLG at :440, asks for the cursor on MONTHLYL at :441 and sends at :442. UNREACHABLE SUCCESS BLOCK (rule R7): SEND-TRNRPT-SCREEN ends GO TO RETURN-TO-CICS at :580 - the program's single GO TO, a benign shared terminal - and RETURN-TO-CICS issues EXEC CICS RETURN at :587, so a send never returns to its caller and the IF NOT ERR-FLG-ON block at :445-456 is never entered: no INITIALIZE-ALL-FIELDS, no DFHGREEN, no 'submitted for printing' notice. Gate G32 does not apply here; CBSTM03A is the only backward-loop program. BYTE ARITHMETIC (B8): the :438 literal is exactly 39 characters; WS-MESSAGE PIC X(80) carries it with 41 trailing spaces, and :560 MOVE WS-MESSAGE TO ERRMSGO is an alphanumeric move into PIC X(78) that truncates on the right, leaving the 39 characters plus 39 spaces. Both channels are reported because reporting only one would make that two-byte loss unobservable. The DISPLAY at :210 is emitted unconditionally on every ENTER path including this one, and it is preserved in the fingerprint rather than dismissed as debug noise (practice B5). The code page is named US-ASCII and never defaulted, and the clock is pinned so the two header items POPULATE-HEADER-INFO builds at :613-628 are comparable byte for byte (practice B7). PRESENTATION, corrected G38: CORPT00C copies neither CSSETATY nor CSSTRPFY - its verified COPY list at :138-149 is COCOM01Y, CORPT00, COTTL01Y, CSDAT01Y, CSMSG01Y, CVTRA05Y, DFHAID and DFHBMSCA - so no field is recoloured red and no '*' marker is written into a blank one. The only colour this program assigns is DFHGREEN at :448, on the success path alone, so ERRMSGC is reported here at the map's default colour, which app/bms/CORPT00.bms declares as COLOR=RED on the ERRMSG DFHMDF at (23,1) LENGTH=78 - declarative, not programmatic. DFHAID and DFHBMSCA are IBM-supplied and absent from this repository (risk R-D), so DFHENTER and the colour mnemonics are read from common.CicsAid and common.BmsAttributes, which reproduce them from IBM CICS documentation. This program touches no dataset - every EXEC CICS in the source is WRITEQ TD, SEND, RECEIVE, RETURN or XCTL - so inputs is empty and gates G16, G19, G21, G45 and G47 have no subject. expectedWrites is empty as a POSITIVE assertion that the job-submission port received nothing: this path never reaches SUBMIT-JOB-TO-INTRDR, so none of the seventeen eighty-byte JCL records is produced (G42 has no subject here). expectedReturnCode is 0 and is stated rather than defaulted - CORPT00C is an online program that sets no RETURN-CODE and contains no CALL 'CEE3ABD', so gate G35 does not apply. The unit is exercised as a CONTROLLER_POJO: the controller is constructed directly and its handler called as a plain method, with no MockMvc, no TestRestTemplate, no servlet container and no HTTP in the path (gate G51), and the whole conversation - commarea, AID and screen values - travels in the payload with no server-side session (rule R6, gate G37). PROVENANCE (practice B12): every expected value here is STATICALLY DERIVED by reading app/cbl/CORPT00C.cbl and cross-checking it against app/cpy-bms/CORPT00.CPY for field widths, app/bms/CORPT00.bms for the declared attributes, app/cpy/COTTL01Y.cpy for the two title literals, app/cpy/CSDAT01Y.cpy for the header date and time shapes and app/cpy/COCOM01Y.cpy for the 160-byte commarea. It was NEVER captured from a running COBOL program, which is empirically impossible in this environment - there is no CICS emulator and the three IBM copybooks are missing (risk R-A). Those reference trees are read-only and were not modified (practice B3), and no value here is a placeholder (practice B1). review_rules reports 'No user rules provided', so zero user rules govern this fixture; the named enterprise practices B1, B3, B5, B7, B8 and B12 are held in their place rather than the bar being lowered.
